counterfactual_missing_items: A core-needle biopsy of the lesion suggested only atrophic mammary glands
the overlying skin was uninvolved and there were no palpable axillary lymph nodes
decisive_items: Six years earlier, she had undergone breast-conserving surgery with endocrine therapy and radiation (50 Gy in 25 fractions) to the left breast for an upper inner quadrant carcinoma.
a 20 mm firm mass fixed to the pectoralis major muscle
On three-month follow-up, the lesion had increased in size.
response.rationale: R1 uniquely integrates prior radiation, a fixed enlarging mass in the irradiated field, and progression despite benign biopsy, fitting radiation-induced sarcoma. R2 is plausible due to prior cancer and growth but is weakened by biopsy showing only atrophic glands and a different quadrant. R3 lacks radiation history; R5's fat necrosis typically does not present as a fixed enlarging mass.

rejected.why: No prior radiation exposure; primary sarcoma is less specific given the strong radiation history.
Fat necrosis would not typically be fixed to muscle and enlarging; imaging and clinical course favor a neoplastic process.
